title: Gamma Point Rows under Quantum Wall Crossing and a Criterion for Stable Irrationality
description: The Gamma integral structure turns the class of a point into a flat covector which reads ordinary rank. This paper asks when the vanishing or nonvanishing of that covector on a formal-monodromy packet is a birational invariant, and reduces the question to one marked continuation problem at each threshold of a single equivariant cobordism. Granting that continuation — a gauged-admissible marked Wlodarczyk completion, together with marked threshold compatibility on every finite Artin truncation of it — X × P^m is irrational for every smooth complex cubic threefold X and every m ≥ 0; only the birational maps X × P^m ⇢ P^(m+3) are ever used. The endpoint contrast is unconditional: the paper reconstructs the primitive-sixth block from Cai's matrices, derives the central charge of the point class from the small I-function, and proves Gamma point-row nonvanishing on both primitive-sixth lines by a Barnes calculation. Multiplication by P^m produces m + 1 copies and preserves detection of the resulting packet, while projective space has no primitive-sixth packet. Detection rather than multiplicity is what has to be transported: through dimension four every blowing-up centre has dimension at most two and carries no primitive-sixth packet, but from m = 2 a centre can be a threefold which carries the packet itself, so that vanishing input is unavailable. Proved outright: an exact ambient point-column identity at a simple VGIT wall, exact Gamma point-row transport across an ordinary flop, global support collapse under the gauged-admissibility assumptions, a coefficientwise balanced Gamma-ratio reduction, and a rank-one derived clutching theorem identifying the fixed clutching stacks, their perfect obstruction theories, and their virtual classes along every affine tail between thresholds, which makes complete neutral tails holonomic with tempered growth. Assumed: an inverse system of one-object marked threshold comparisons over all finite Artin levels, ordinary degrees, neutral directions, and thresholds. At each threshold one marked local Fourier object must induce an isomorphism of the adjacent finite cyclic Rees z-differential modules which intertwines formal monodromy, carries the marked point row, and preserves the stated Stokes, deck, Artin, and Rees data; at a zero mode the comparison is taken on reduced nearby cycles and must identify the entire adjacent row-generated module with its reduced realization. Given those maps the transport is linear algebra. A marked Gamma/window continuation conjecture, new to this paper, would imply both hypotheses and is the route by which they are expected to be removed. A rational two-tail counterexample and the incomplete-Gamma and Fourier-boundary countermodels explain why tailwise holonomicity, formal monodromy, pairing, integrality, and localized Fourier support do not replace that marked compatibility.
